en: Paṭṭhānapakaraṇa:
Dhammapaccanīya (2), Dukadukapaṭṭhānapāḷi (6) 12.1.
Hetuduka, Sahetukadukādi (The Dyads on Roots, beginning with the Dyad on Being Accompanied by a Root)
Homage to that Blessed One, the Worthy One, the Perfectly Self-Awakened One.
Dependent on a state that is neither-root nor accompanied-by-root, a state that is neither-root nor accompanied-by-root arises by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated.
Three for root; one for object … pe … one for result … pe … three for non-disappearance.
Dependent on a state that is neither a root nor accompanied by a root, there arises a state that is neither a root nor accompanied by a root, by way of non-root condition (*nahetupaccaya*).
Dependent on a state that is neither a root nor accompanied by a root, there arises a state that is neither a root nor accompanied by a root, by way of non-object condition (*naārammaṇapaccaya*).

(Abbreviated. Under non-root: one; under non-object: three; under non-predominance: three ... pe ... under non-kamma: one ... pe ... under non-nutriment, non-faculty, non-jhāna, and non-path: one ... pe ... under non-disappearance: three.
A state that is neither-root nor accompanied-by-root is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a state that is neither-root nor accompanied-by-root.
A state that is neither-root nor accompanied-by-root is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state that is neither-root nor accompanied-by-root.
A state that is neither-root nor rootless is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state that is neither-root nor rootless.
(Abbreviated. Under root: one; under object: four; under proximity: four … pe … under conascence: three; under mutuality: one;
under dependence and strong-dependence: four; under prenascence, postnascence, and repetition: two; under kamma … pe … under jhāna: one.
With respect to association, one; with respect to dissociation, three ... pe ... with respect to non-disappearance, four.
Dependent on a state that is neither-root nor rootless, there arises a state that is neither-root nor rootless by way of root-condition.
Dependent on a state that is neither-root nor rootless, there arises a state that is not-non-root and not-rootless by way of root-condition.
Dependent on a state that is neither-root nor rootless, there arise states that are neither-root nor rootless and states that are not-root but not rootless by way of root-condition.
Dependent on a state that is not-root but not rootless, there arises a state that is not-root but not rootless by way of root-condition.
Dependent on a state that is neither a root-cause nor rootless, there arises a state that is neither a root-cause nor rootless by way of root-condition.
Dependent on a state that is neither a root-cause nor rootless, there arise states that are both neither a root-cause nor rootless and neither a root-cause nor rootless by way of root-condition.
Dependent on a state that is neither-root nor rootless and a state that is neither-non-root nor non-rootless, there arises a state that is neither-root nor rootless by way of root-condition.
Dependent on a state that is neither-root nor rootless and a state that is neither-non-root nor non-rootless, there arises a state that is neither-non-root nor non-rootless by way of root-condition.
Dependent on a state that is neither-root nor rootless and a state that is neither-non-root nor non-rootless...
Dependent on a state that is neither a root nor non-root, both states that are neither roots nor non-roots and those that are neither roots nor non-roots arise by way of the root condition.
(Abbreviated. Nine in the case of the root; nine in the case of the object … pe … nine in the case of non-disappearance. (Nine in all cases.
Dependent on a state that is not a root and is dissociated from roots, a state that is not a root and is dissociated from roots arises by way of the root condition … three. (Abbreviated.)

With respect to the root condition (hetu), there are three; with respect to the object condition (ārammaṇa), one ... pe ... with respect to the result condition (vipāka), one ... pe ... with respect to the non-disappearance condition (avigata), three.
In dependence on a state that is neither-root nor dissociated from root, a state that is neither-root nor dissociated from root arises by way of the root condition ... three.
In dependence on a state that is not-non-root and dissociated from root, a state that is not-non-root and dissociated from root arises by way of the root condition ... three.

Dependent on a state that is neither-root nor dissociated from root, and [dependent on] a state that is neither-root nor dissociated from root, there arises a state that is neither-root nor dissociated from root by way of root-condition … three. (Abbreviated. Nine under root;
… pe … nine under non-disappearance. (Full detail everywhere.

Dependent on a state that is neither-root and also neither-root, and a state that is not rootless, there arises a state that is neither-root and also not rootless by way of root-condition. (This continues until even in the section of questions there is one.)

Dependent on a state that is neither-with-root-cause-nor-rootless as well as a state that is not a root-cause, there arises a state that is neither-with-root-cause-nor-rootless as well as a state that is not a root-cause, by way of root-condition. (In all cases, one.

Dependent on a state that is not a root-cause and a state that is both not a root-cause and dissociated from a root-cause, there arises a state that is not a root-cause and a state that is both not a root-cause and dissociated from a root-cause, by way of root-condition. (In all cases, one.)

Dependent on a state that is neither-with-root-cause nor dissociated from root-cause and is also not-root-cause, there arises a state that is neither-with-root-cause nor dissociated from root-cause and is also not-root-cause, by way of root-condition. (In all cases, one.

Dependent on a state that is not-root-cause and not-accompanied-by-root-cause, there arises a state that is not-root-cause and not-accompanied-by-root-cause, by way of root-condition. (In all cases, one.
Dependent on a state that is not-root-cause and not-rootless, there arises a state that is not-root-cause and not-rootless, by way of root-condition. (In all cases, one.)
